question.text: Categorization of algorithms into 'White box' and 'Black box' is based on:

answer.text: Whether the workings and rationale of the algorithm are transparent (White box) or opaque (Black box)
Whether the algorithm trades in agricultural or non-agricultural commodities

explanation.text: The Logic: The White box versus Black box table on pages 124-125 shows that White box logic and workings are transparent to users, while Black box workings and rationale are not accessible. The Trap: Execution speed, commodity type (agricultural vs non-agricultural), and order size are not the distinguishing criteria; the transparency of the algorithm's logic is. Note: The source distinguishes provider registration from algo registration: the Black box algo provider must register as a Research Analyst, and each Black box logic change should be registered as a new algo with exchange confirmation.
